MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  October 22, 2019

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Pro Tem Goodell at 5:02 p.m., on October 8, 2019, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on October 17, 2019, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and Norman P.
Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Sachs
  Mayor Pro Tem Goodell
  Mayor Raths (arrived at 5:15 p.m.)

Absent:  None

Staff Present: Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Liability Claims: Claimants: Donaldson, Orloff, Gray, O’Brien and Peterson: Agency
  Claimed Against-City of Mission Viejo and: Significant Exposure to Litigation
  Pursuant to Paragraph (2) of Subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9. (5 cases).

RECESS AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:03 p.m. Mayor Pro Tem Goodell recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The
City Council reconvened in the Council Chamber at 6:00 p.m. with all five City Council Members
present.

City Council Minutes  1  October 22, 2019
 REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the City Council received updates on claims and pending
litigation in Closed Session. The Council gave direction to staff, but no reportable actions
occurred.

INVOCATION: Council Member Bucknum

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Raths

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Adopted Headquarters Battalion of the 1st Marine Division Quarterly Recognition

  The Mayor presented certificates of commendation to "Marine of the Quarter" Lance
  Corporal Matthew Booth and "Noncommissioned Officer of the Quarter" Corporal Calvin
  Beal.

P2. Featured Businesses of the Month - Lock-Tech and the inside coup

  The Mayor Presented proclamations to Randy Johnson and Tricia Yee.

P3. Vector Control Report

  Vector Control Board Member Bob Ruesch provided an update.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Robert Breton, M.V.: Congratulated the City Council on the acquisition of the Casta del Sol Golf
Course. He commended the City Manager and staff for their astute decision on the purchase.
Robert also suggested the re-naming of the golf course to “Oso Creek Golf Course.”

Randy Johnson, Lock-Tech, Rancho Santa Margarita: Thanked the Council for their service and
discussed how residents can secure sliding glass doors from potential break-ins.

Ingmar Forster, M.V.: Agreed with the re-naming of Casta del Sol Golf Course to Oso Creek Golf
Course. He inquired on the status of the California Voting Rights Act lawsuit and expressed
concerns regarding the City's stand on whether it will exercise cumulative voting or go to district
voting in the November 2020 Election.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None
City Council Minutes  2  October 22, 2019
 1.  City Council Minutes

  (1) Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of October 8, 2019, as
  presented; and (2) approved the Minutes for the adjourned City Council Meeting of October
  14, 2019, as presented.

2.  Check Register Dated September 27, 2019 in the Amount of $1,221,073.01

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  Check Register Dated October 4, 2019 in the Amount of $1,266,129.15

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for August 2019

  Received and filed.

5.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer’s
  Monthly Report for August 2019

  Received and filed.

6.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for August
  2019

  Received and filed.

7.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly Report
  for August 2019

  Received and filed.

9.  Donations of Surplus Property to Mercy House

  Authorized staff to donate surplus property to Mercy House on an as-needed basis.

10. Prop 68 Per Capita Grant Application - Craycraft Park Improvements

  Adopted Resolution 19-39 Approving the Submittal of an Application to the State of
  California Department of Parks and Recreation for Funding Under the California Drought,
  Water, Parks, Climate, Coastal Protection, and Outdoor Access for All Act (Prop 68) for
  Craycraft Park Improvements

11. Additional Geotechnical Feasibility and Mass Grading Services for Lower Curtis Park

  Issued a purchase order to GMU Geotechnical in an amount not to exceed $79,500 for
  geotechnical feasibility and mass grading plan design services for Lower Curtis Park
  Expansion Project.
City Council Minutes  3  October 22, 2019
 12. Cancellation of the November 26, 2019 City Council Meeting

  Approved the cancellation of the November 26, 2019 City Council Meeting.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

8.  Residential Trash Rate Adjustment

  Environmental Program Administrator Denise Matson presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to adopt
  Resolution 19-38 Approving the Proposed Trash Rate Adjustment for Residential Trash
  Service (From $14.71 to $16.95 per Month) Effective January 1, 2020.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

OLD BUSINESS

13. City of Mission Viejo Comprehensive Bikeway and Transportation Connectivity
  Master Plan

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Ratty presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to
  approve the Bikeway Master Plan.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

14. Loan Agreement Between the City and the Section 115 Pension Trust Fund

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to adopt
  Approved loan agreement between the City and the Section 115 Pension Trust Fund in the
  amount of $1,000,000.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
City Council Minutes  4  October 22, 2019
 15. Service Animal Licensing

  Animal Services Manager Michelle Claud-Clemente gave the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Raths, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to approve the
  changes to Animal Service Licensing.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

16. Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Council Member Sachs asked Fire Chief Capobianco for an update on fire conditions in the
  City.

17. Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Received report from Council Member Kelley.

18. Orange County Local Agency Formation Commission (LAFCO) Report

  Received report from Council Member Bucknum.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as
presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum announced that she attended the “Tee It Up for Marines” Golf
Tournament at Camp Pendleton. She thanked all the volunteers that came out to support the event
and she thanked AYSO Region 84, Mission Viejo Country Club, Casta del Sol, Shea Homes and
Waste Management for their participation as well. The tournament supports the Marine Corps Ball
and helps lower ticket prices for the Marines and their wives or dates. She further discussed her
attendance at the DAWG Walk and said she enjoyed the Halloween Parade of Dogs. Council
Member Bucknum also attended the Drug Walk and she suggested that more bands be invited to
participate in the parade. She announced that on Monday she attended the Special Meeting of the
Southern California Association of Government’s (SCAG), Community, Economic and Human
Development Committee (CEHD), where a determination and recommendation to SCAG was
made on the Regional Housing Needs Allocation (RHNA) Housing Methodology. Council
Member Bucknum asked the City Manager to post the article that she had written, along with
City Council Minutes  5  October 22, 2019
 Consultant Gail Shiomoto-Lohr, to the City’s website so that residents can be informed of the
housing mandates and how the State is going to allocate housing demands to cities. She said she’ll
also post it to her public Facebook account. Lastly, Council Member Bucknum stated that she
hopes to see everyone at the Veterans Day Ceremony on November 11 at the Norman P. Murray
Community Center.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley announced that she too attended the “Tee It Up for Marines” Golf
Tournament and she said it was a huge success. She thanked the Marine Adoption Committee, her
husband Jack, and Carol and Chuck Weidler. Council Member Kelley encouraged the public to
donate any unused prom or bridesmaid dresses to the City for the wives and girlfriends of the
Marines to wear to the Marine Corps Ball. She noted that the first Drug Abuse Expo was held at
Norman P. Murray Community Center and was a success. She received very good feedback and
she thanked the Character Committee and Drug Prevention Coalition for their efforts. Council
Member Kelley announced that the Drug Abuse Awareness Plaque dedication will take place on
Tuesday, October 29, from 3:00 p.m. to 4:00 p.m. at Lakeside Park which is on the corner of
Marguerite Parkway and Alicia Parkway. The plaque serves as a reminder of the young lives that
have been lost to drug overdose. Council Member Kelley stated that the Walk Against Drugs was
a really big success and she felt there was a larger audience than in previous years. She credited
Chief Vuong on the success of the event and praised his “Safe Schools Challenge” where schools
compete against each other, sharing the message of living drug free. Council Member Kelley also
thanked Crime Prevention Specialists Khatra Molina and Paula Monical for leading this event
along with the keynote speaker, Deputy Aron Grumbles. Lastly, she announced that on Monday
November 18, 2019, there will be a blood drive at City Hall from 12:00 p.m. to 6:00 p.m. She
encouraged residents to donate blood as there is a shortage and she asked anyone interested in
volunteering to head the staffing of the blood drive to call or email her and she will provide
information for specifics of the volunteer job.

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs announced that he had no comments this evening.

Mayor Pro Tem Goodell

Mayor Pro Tem Goodell mentioned that he attended many of the same events as his fellow Council
Members and his dogs, Max and Lucy, attended the DAWG Walk with him and enjoyed it. Mayor
Pro Tem Goodell announced that the Judy and Bill Leonard Institute for Cancer Prevention &
Research will be having its Grand Opening on November 7. Lastly, he stated that he is looking
forward to the Marine Corps Ball.

Mayor Raths

19. Update on CIP Projects

  Kraig Erickson, M.V.: Voiced his concern over funding of upcoming CIP projects now that
  the City bought the Casta del Sol Golf Course. He asked how these smaller projects are going
  to be funded if surplus monies went towards the golf course.

City Council Minutes  6  October 22, 2019
   By consensus the Council asked staff to bring this item back at the next meeting.

Mayor Raths announced that on Wednesday, November 6, 2019, the grand reveal of the Fallen
Soldier Memorial will be held at Lakeside Park from 10:00 a.m. to 11:00 a.m.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 7:56 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Raths adjourned the meeting in memory of General J.K. Davis USMC (RET)
to Tuesday, November 12, 2019, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________
Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of November 12, 2019

City Council Minutes  7  October 22, 2019
